name: Martin Luther
role: Augustinian friar, professor of theology, reformer

born.place: Eisleben, County of Mansfeld, Holy Roman Empire

summary: German friar and professor whose challenge to the sale of indulgences in 1517 sparked the Protestant Reformation and whose German Bible shaped both the church and the German language.

key_dates.label: Caught in a thunderstorm, vows to become a monk; enters the Augustinian friary at Erfurt
Receives doctorate in theology; becomes professor at Wittenberg
Writes the Ninety-five Theses against indulgences (31 October)
Publishes three major reform treatises; burns the papal bull
Excommunicated; refuses to recant at the Diet of Worms
Publishes his German New Testament ("September Testament")

accomplishments.text: Wrote the Ninety-five Theses (1517) disputing the sale of indulgences, which spread rapidly by printing and started the Reformation.
Taught that sinners are justified before God by grace through faith alone, not by works or purchased merit.
In 1520 published To the Christian Nobility of the German Nation, The Babylonian Captivity of the Church, and The Freedom of a Christian.
Refused to recant his writings before Emperor Charles V at the Diet of Worms (April 1521) unless convinced by Scripture and plain reason.
Translated the New Testament into German while hidden at the Wartburg castle (published 1522), and with colleagues completed the whole Bible by 1534.
Married the former nun Katharina von Bora (1525), modeling a married Protestant clergy.
Wrote The Bondage of the Will (1525) in reply to Erasmus on free will and grace.
Wrote the Small and Large Catechisms (1529) for teaching families and pastors, and many hymns including "A Mighty Fortress Is Our God."

sources.citation: Luther's Works, American Edition, ed. Jaroslav Pelikan and Helmut T. Lehmann, 55 vols. (St. Louis: Concordia; Philadelphia: Fortress, 1955–1986).
Roland H. Bainton, Here I Stand: A Life of Martin Luther (New York: Abingdon-Cokesbury, 1950).
Heiko A. Oberman, Luther: Man between God and the Devil, trans. Eileen Walliser-Schwarzbart (New Haven: Yale University Press, 1989).
